H1.scientific_argument: This model proposes a power-law relationship between temperature and the log-corrosion rate. It serves as a more flexible local approximation than a simple linear model, allowing for either accelerating (exponent > 1) or decelerating (exponent < 1) increase in corrosion rate with temperature. It acts as a phenomenological rival to the mechanistically-derived Arrhenius form, testing whether a simple power law can capture the observed trend within the experimental temperature range.
H1.evidence_gap: This is a phenomenological closure. It does not derive from a specific physical mechanism, but provides a flexible functional form to test against the Arrhenius law and simpler linear approximations.
H1.mathematical_distinction: A power-law dependence on temperature (tau^p1) as opposed to the exponential dependence on inverse temperature (exp(-1/tau)) of the Arrhenius model or the linear dependence (tau) of the local linear model. The additional parameter `p1` allows for both concave and convex shapes, providing more flexibility than the fixed-shape linear or logarithmic models.

question_links.observable_prediction: The logarithm of the corrosion current will follow a power-law relationship with absolute temperature.

H1.scientific_argument: This model proposes a logarithmic relationship, suggesting that the promotional effect of temperature on corrosion has diminishing returns. This could phenomenologically represent a scenario where the initial increase in kinetic rates is significant, but the effect lessens as other factors become rate-limiting. It provides a simple, monotonically increasing rival to the Arrhenius law with a different curvature (strictly concave).
H1.evidence_gap: This is a phenomenological closure. The logarithmic form is chosen for its mathematical properties (monotonic, concave) rather than being derived from a specific theory of temperature effects.
H1.mathematical_distinction: A logarithmic dependence on temperature (log(tau)), which is always concave (diminishing returns). This contrasts with the linear model (constant returns) and the Arrhenius model (convex dependence on tau).

question_links.observable_prediction: The logarithm of the corrosion current will increase with the logarithm of the absolute temperature.
